content:
Semantics: Small-Step Operational Semantics for Integer Expressions with abs

1. Syntax
    Integer expressions e are given by the grammar:

        e ::= n                    integer literals        n in Z
            | abs(e)               absolute value
            | e1 + e2              addition
            | e1 - e2              subtraction

    Integer values v are the literals:

        v ::= n                    (n in Z)

    Note: a value is a particular kind of expression; every value is
    an expression, and values are exactly the expressions that cannot
    take a step.

2. Evaluation Relation
    The small-step evaluation relation  e --> e'  ("e steps to e'")
    is the smallest relation on expressions closed under the
    inference rules below.

    Notation: s(x) denotes the successor of x (x + 1); -x denotes the
    additive inverse of x; n1 + n2 denotes the (mathematical) sum of
    the integers n1 and n2.

3. Inference Rules

    Congruence rules (evaluate subexpressions first):

        (S-PlusLeft)                (S-PlusRight)
        e1 --> e1'                  v1 value    e2 --> e2'
        ---------------------       -------------------------
        e1 + e2 --> e1' + e2        v1 + e2 --> v1 + e2'

        (S-MinusLeft)               (S-MinusRight)
        e1 --> e1'                  v1 value    e2 --> e2'
        ---------------------       -------------------------
        e1 - e2 --> e1' - e2        v1 - e2 --> v1 - e2'

        (S-Abs)
        e --> e'
        -------------------
        abs(e) --> abs(e')

    Value/computation rules for abs (one step per literal):

        (S-AbsZero)
        -------------
        abs(0) --> 0

        (S-AbsPos)
        -------------
        abs(s(n)) --> s(n)          for every non-negative n

        (S-AbsNeg)
        --------------
        abs(-s(n)) --> s(n)         for every non-negative n

    Computation rules for arithmetic:

        (S-Plus)                    (S-Minus)
        -------------               -----------------------------
        n1 + n2 --> (n1 + n2)       n1 - n2 --> (n1 - n2)

4. Evaluation to a Value (Multi-Step)
    Multi-step evaluation  e -->* v  is the reflexive-transitive
    closure of --> :

        (S-Refl)                    (S-Trans)
        --------                    e --> e'    e' -->* v
        e -->* e                    ------------------------
                                    e -->* v

5. Derived Results

    5.1 Normal forms. The normal forms of this semantics are exactly
        the integer literals n. Every well-formed expression either
        is a value or can take a step, so --> is progress-complete.

    5.2 Determinism. If e --> e1 and e --> e2, then e1 = e2. Each rule
        applies to a disjoint syntactic shape, and each rule's
        conclusion fixes the result uniquely, hence --> is a partial
        function.

    5.3 Semantics of abs. For every integer x:

            abs(x) -->* y   if and only if   (y = x and x >= 0)
                                          or (y = -x and x < 0)

        In particular, by rule (S-AbsZero), abs(0) -->* 0, so the
        two cases x >= 0 and x < 0 agree at x = 0, matching the
        specification in spec.txt (P2, P3).

    5.4 Termination. Every step strictly reduces the number of
        operators (abs, +, -) in the expression; congruence rules
        preserve this count and computation rules decrease it.
        Hence every expression reduces to a unique value.

6. Soundness w.r.t. spec.txt
    Define the denotation [[e]] of an expression in the obvious way
    ([[n]] = n, [[abs(e)]] = |[[e]]|, etc., with |.| as specified in
    spec.txt). Then for all expressions e and values v:

        e -->* v   implies   [[e]] = v

    i.e., the operational semantics is sound with respect to the
    mathematical specification of the absolute value function.
